thread:
rachel: Heads up — our py-sdk sample app hits a nasty spike of 429s when rotating short-lived tokens while prefetching pages. Repro in CI. anyone seen token-rotation + paginator issues?

ajay: which py-sdk version and pagination mode (cursor vs offset)?

rachel: python client 1.4.0, using cursor-based paging + background prefetch with max_inflight=12. Token rotation every 45s (STS). 429s start ~300ms after rotation and last ~10-30s.

tom: can you paste the minimal flow? curious if old inflight requests are retried with new token or aborted.

rachel: snippet:```py
# simplified prefetcher
while True:
    while inflight < max_inflight and has_next:
        inflight += 1
        schedule(fetch_page(cursor)).add_done_callback(lambda f: inflight -=1)

# auth rotate handler
def on_refresh(token):
    client.update_token(token)
    # we don't stop prefetch or cancel inflight
```

token-bot: logged headers around failure: x-ratelimit-limit:200, x-ratelimit-remaining:0, x-ratelimit-reset:2623460200, x-client-session:py:session_77

ajay: sounds like the server sees many new connections/identities after rotation (session fingerprint changes) + prefetch immediately pushes next pages. server enforces per-session rate so a bunch of 'new' sessions exceed per-session quota.

rachel: we tried toggling backoff (linear backoff after 429) but the first burst is enough to tank the quota and cause cascading retries.

tom: couple ideas: 1) pause the prefetch loop for a small cool-down after token rotate; 2) reuse the same HTTP connection pool/agent so session id persists; 3) make token rotation atomic with in-flight request draining or graceful token propagation.

rachel: quick patch: pause prefetch for 2s and reuse requests.Session() across token swaps. 429s dropped ~70% in my run but still see spikes with concurrency=12.

ajay: are you cancelling inflight requests when updating token? that reduces duplicated work. Also consider jitter on resume.

rachel: we weren't cancelling. Cancelling on rotate plus randomized 100-600ms delay before resuming reduced 429s to negligible in staging.

devdocs: can we add a "Auth rotation guidance" recipe to py-sdk docs? Suggest: reuse session/pool, pause/resume prefetch, cancel in-flight when possible, and add jittered backoff. I'll draft PR #4721.

tom: also file-level: we should check server session keying to understand whether token fingerprinting is necessary or if we can allow sticky session mapping by client-id header. I'll open a ticket to prod infra.

rachel: dropping repro + logs to the thread: link (internal). happy to have eng-run it against staging traces.

ajay: great repro, I'll run it and attach traces. thanks for the clear steps. :thumbsup:
